evidence.claim: Cardholder C08106 explicitly denies the $128.33 charge 3583227 ('I never made this purchase'), a customer_report trigger opened 2016-12-29.
Flagged amount $128.33 is 3.63x the 180-day mean of $35.31 (std $27.72, z=3.36) over 209 transactions, just under the card max of $138.89.

Flagged txn used device 'unknown | unknown | firefox 47.0 | unknown', not in this card's history and marked New for the account; the card's usual devices are Windows/chrome 63.0 (22 txns) and similar.

A second anomalous online charge 3580804 for $92.86 (2.63x mean, New device flag, gmail domain vs hotmail on the flagged txn) occurred 23.5h earlier on 2016-12-28, forming a 2-transaction burst within 48h totalling $221.19.

Prior closed case CC-3778 on this same card C08106-K1 was a confirmed card_not_present_fraud ($58.42, single unrecognized online purchase inconsistent with usual merchants/amounts), showing this card number has been compromised before.

Counter-evidence: CC-0696 on the same card was cleared after the cardholder confirmed travel, and five semantically similar cases (CC-0865, CC-5164, CC-3168, CC-3465, CC-0893) were cleared as genuine purchases from a new phone - so the New-device flag alone is not proof.

The flagged device profile appears on only 6 cards all-time and 1 card in the window, so it does not establish a shared-origin ring; the heavily shared strings in cards_linked_by_rare_device (e.g. 'Windows | unknown | firefox 60.0 | unknown', 39 cards) are generic and not used by this transaction.

Policy R2 applies: the customer denies the transaction, so BLOCK_CARD and CREATE_CASE are indicated; exposure of $221.19 is below $1,000 and there is no solid shared-device link, so no regulatory report is required.

case.summary: C08106 disputes a $128.33 online purchase (3583227) made 2016-12-29 from a browser profile never seen on card C08106-K1 and flagged New for the account. The amount is 3.6x the cardholder's $35.31 average across 209 all-online transactions, and it is paired with a $92.86 charge the previous day (3580804) from another New device and a different email domain - a classic two-transaction CNP burst within 48 hours. This card already has a confirmed card-not-present fraud in memory (CC-3778), which makes re-use of a leaked number plausible. The rare-device graph links are generic strings and do not tie this episode to a specific ring, so exposure stays at $221.19 on this card alone. Recommend blocking the card and opening a case; a regulatory report is not warranted at this exposure without a shared-origin link.

stop_reason: Further evidence unlikely to change the decision; no new policy-approved request remains (p=0.82, confidence 0.87; policy §6). Four independent signals (explicit cardholder denial, unseen/New device, 3.4-sigma amount, a matching same-shape charge 23h earlier) plus a prior confirmed CNP fraud on this exact card support a fraud verdict; a verification request would only restate the dispute the customer has already made, so further steps are unlikely to change the block decision.
